messages:
Leo Zhang: quick onboarding hiccup — ran the curl install on a shared devbox and redwoodctl ended up in /opt/redwood/bin which wasn't on PATH. new dev confused.
Tara Singh: installer should follow XDG/USER conventions or honor --install-dir. We used to surface an "add to PATH" snippet after install.
Mateo Ruiz: another thing: the installer auto-triggers `redwoodctl login`. On CI runners that opens a browser and just hangs the job. Could we make auto-login opt-in? --auto-login flag maybe.
Leo Zhang: repro: `curl -fsSL https://install.redwood.ai | sh` then stuck at "Opening browser..." in a minimal container.
Tara Singh: agreed. also saw token storage oddness: on Fedora the credential helper returned success but `redwoodctl config list` showed <none> for LAST_LOGIN. The helper claims write but libsecret not available in headless images.
Mateo Ruiz: workaround for now: `redwoodctl login --store=file --file-path="$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/creds.json"` and mount that file in CI.
Leo Zhang: FYI `redwoodctl auth status` returned "no credentials" immediately after login. There is a small window where the helper commits async. Scripts fail if they start `redwoodctl local serve` immediately.
Tara Singh: we should add a `--wait` flag to login that blocks until the store commit is verified. short-term: poll `redwoodctl auth status` in onboarding scripts.
ci-bot: NOTE: CI image bump scheduled. image will include /usr/local/bin in PATH and will set REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1 by default.
Mateo Ruiz: one more: precedence bug: flags vs config file. `redwoodctl local serve --profile=staging` was ignored when serve.yaml had profile: default. The config file was taking precedence unexpectedly.
Tara Singh: opened issue #487 to fix precedence (CLI flags > env > config file).
Leo Zhang: adding a tiny snippet to docs for now:
```
# non-sudo install
curl -fsSL https://install.redwood.ai | sh -s -- --install-dir "$HOME/.local/bin"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# headless login for CI
export REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1
redwoodctl login --device-code --store=file --file-path="$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/creds.json"

# wait for credentials before serving
until redwoodctl auth status --profile=staging; do sleep 0.5; done
redwoodctl local serve --profile=staging
```
Mateo Ruiz: perfect. tagging docs to include this and the env var. :thumbsup:
